claims.text: Adding a small amount of a sintering aid that forms a transient liquid phase will reduce the temperature required for full ceramic densification.
A low-concentration metal oxide or phosphate can form a liquid phase at lower temperatures when added to ceramic powder.
The sintering aid produces a transient liquid phase at particle boundaries during sintering.
The sintering aid lowers grain-boundary energy.
Formation of a short-lived liquid phase enhances mass transport.
Enhanced mass transport through the transient liquid phase promotes rapid densification at lower temperatures than conventional solid-state sintering.
The doped ceramic will achieve densification comparable to the undoped ceramic at a significantly lower sintering temperature.
The doped ceramic will achieve microstructural development comparable to the undoped ceramic at a significantly lower sintering temperature.
Ceramic powders without sintering aids require higher temperatures for full densification.
The effectiveness of a sintering aid depends on its concentration, compatibility with the base material, and the ceramic system.
Excessive sintering-aid concentration or incompatibility with the ceramic can adversely affect microstructure or properties.
